outcome: frequency of elective and emergency cesarean sections
cohort: 7100 pregnant women in Berlin, Germany, of which 3765 had a migration background
finding: In Berlin, among migrant women, a low degree of acculturation may have an unfavorable effect on the utilization of pregnancy care provision, but there were no relevant differences in obstetric outcome parameters in relation to the degree of acculturation.
mod_finding: The study found no significant difference in the frequency of elective and emergency cesarean sections between migrant women with different degrees of acculturation.
